# dsh-subagent-tiering
Subagents run on a cheaper sibling of the parent model unless the agent names a route.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Subagents run on a cheaper sibling of the parent's model unless the main agent
names a route itself.
## Install
Install from npm: `dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-subagent-tiering`, or from GitHub:
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-subagent-tiering`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` lists it in `dsh.profile.bundles` and
its own

patch inserts the `subagent-tiering` entry with the built-in rules. A local checkout
works too: `ds

h plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-subagent-tiering`.
Requires Node 22.18 or newe

r; used on DSH 0.1.5 and 0.2.1. Read "Needs" below: without a
subagent model-selection policy the pl
ugin changes nothing.
| Parent route | Child default |
| anthropic Opus / Fable / Sonnet | anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5` @ medium (falls back to `claude-so

nnet-5`) |
| alibaba Qwen max/plus | `qwen3.8-flash` @ high |
| alibaba / byteplus DeepSeek pro | th

e provider's DeepSeek flash @ high |
| byteplus GLM / Seed | `glm-5-3-flash-260828` @ high |
| deeps

eek-official | `deepseek-flash` @ high |
| mistral large | `mistral-medium-latest` |
| any other mis

tral, alibaba GLM, hetzner | same model, effort capped at high (never raised) |
| anything else | in
herits the parent, as stock dsh does |

`vision-toolkit-<x>` parents keep their wrapper provider. Rules live in
`src/rules.js` and can be ov

erridden with a `- id: subagent-tiering` row in the
profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (`config.rules`, sa

ith a `- id: subagent-tiering` row in the
profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (`config.rules`, same shape).

A rule's `child.fallbackModels` (optional list of model ids, same provider and
effort) is tried in o

rder when the primary model is not in the chat's captured
allow-list or does not resolve. 2026-09-29

: the Anthropic default moved from
Sonnet 5 to Sonnet 5.5; chats created before that day have no Son

net 5.5 in
their allow-list, so they keep getting Sonnet 5 instead of inheriting Opus.

Over 14 days of session logs on one busy install, 70% of dsh's Anthropic calls were
subagents. The s

tock `ptc` preset gives `subagent` no child defaults, so every
child ran on the parent's route and e

ffort (usually Opus 5.5 at max). Per human
prompt, dsh cost 2.1x what Claude Code did on the same bo

x, while per call the
two were about equal. `tool-subagent`'s own `agentOptions` is one static route
and cannot express "Opus parent → Sonnet child, Qwen parent → Qwen-flash child".
## How it works

A `tools/pre-execute` handler. When a `subagent` call names no `provider`,
`model` or `reasoning_eff

ort`, it fills them in from the first matching rule, as
if the model had asked. The stock tool then

runs its normal checks. It leaves the
call untouched, so the child inherits the parent, when:

- the main agent passed any of the three fields itself (its choice always wins);
- the chat has no m

odel-selection policy. dsh records one only for chats created
while `subagent-model-selection.enable

icy's `allowedModels`;
- `llm.resolveCallConfig` rejects the route. If it rejects only the effort, t

rt is dropped and the route kept;
- core dsh ever freezes the execution record. This is logged once.

`subagent_fork` is never touched. A fork must stay on the parent route to reuse
its cached prefix.

A short system-prompt section (`subagent-tiering`, about 90 tokens) tells the
model about the defaul
t and how to override it.
### Trade-off

A child on a different model cannot reuse the parent's prompt cache, so its
first call pays a full c

ache write (about 48k tokens on Anthropic after the GenUI
removal). A one-call subagent can therefor

e cost slightly more than before. The
median subagent here makes 28 calls, so it comes out well ahea

cost slightly more than before. The
median subagent here makes 28 calls, so it comes out well ahead.
## Needs

- settings `subagent-model-selection: { enabled: true, allowedModels: [...] }`.
On DSH 0.2.x this ha

rness setting lives under the entry
`subagent-model-selection-settings` and is not imported from an

old `settings.yaml`
(see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md).
- the `ptc` / `ptc-lean` preset's `tool-subagent`

row with
`modelSelectionSettings: true` (stock).
- adaptive-reasoning must NOT list `anthropic/clau

de-sonnet-5-5` (or
`claude-sonnet-5`, the fallback) among its routes,
or it would override the child
's medium effort on every step.
## Verify

`node --test test/*.test.js` runs the unit tests. End to end: start a new chat on
Opus 5.5 and have

it call `subagent` with no model. The child session's
`request/header` shows `claude-sonnet-5-5` / `

medium` (was `claude-sonnet-5`
until 2026-09-29). Checked on 2026-09-27 on
a production install (Opu

s → Sonnet) and in a sandbox (Qwen max → Qwen flash; an explicit
`qwen3.8-max @ low` was left as ask

Sonnet) and in a sandbox (Qwen max → Qwen flash; an explicit
`qwen3.8-max @ low` was left as asked).
## When something goes wrong

- Ask your agent to load the **`subagent-tiering-doctor`** skill (copy
`skills/subagent-tiering-doct

or` into `~/.dsh/skills/` once,
how).
- Symptom-first guide: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md.
- Log lines an
d start-up messages: docs/ERRORS.md.
